findings.reason: The protected app-local and Accepted native sources use the conventional iterative inorder traversal, retain one unfinished root-to-leaf path, decrement the rank exactly once per visited node, and return immediately at the requested rank. The implementation is clear, concise, O(h + k)-time, and O(h)-space, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local function and native class method have identical stack initialization, left-path descent, pop/decrement order, early return, and right-subtree transition. The app-local TreeNode class is the required standalone equivalent of LeetCode's injected model.

The former benchmark selected k = n, making an O(n)-time full inorder materialization indistinguishable from the claimed early-stop bound. The same legal 31/127/511-node balanced trees now select k = 1. The protected source passes at -0.01 relative exponent; a correct full-traversal implementation passes every output and fails only scaling at +0.77 with an 18.21x largest runtime ratio.

The Approach accurately derives rank order from BST inorder traversal and bounds pushes plus pops by O(h + k). It now avoids referring to the decremented counter as the original rank and labels the skewed-tree/extreme-rank boundary explicitly.
